title: Gravitational, Electric and Magnetic Fields

key_big: Gravity and electric force both follow an inverse-square law.
body_html:
How to think about it

Newton's law of universal gravitation: F = Gm₁m₂/r² with G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N·m²/kg². Doubling the distance gives a quarter of the force. For a circular orbit, gravity provides the centripetal force: Gm/r = v².

Coulomb's law F = kq₁q₂/r² (k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N·m²/C²) has the same form, but charges can repel as well as attract. The electric field ε = F/q points the way a positive charge would move. A charge moving through a magnetic field feels F = qvB sin θ; a current feels F = BIL sin θ.

Example

Two charges are moved three times as far apart. The force becomes?

Inverse square: 1/3²

Answer: 1/9 as large

Example

A proton (q = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C) moves at 2.0 × 10⁶ m/s at right angles to a 0.50 T field. Force?

F = qvB

Answer: 1.6 × 10⁻¹³ N

Common mistakes

  • Using r as the distance from the surface instead of from the centre of a planet.
  • Forgetting to square the distance.
  • Thinking a magnetic field does work on a moving charge: the force is always at right angles to the motion.

faq.a: They and their craft are falling around Earth together, with gravity giving the centripetal acceleration.
